submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L1 at a 37 GeV threshold as the highest-efficiency choice supported by the available rate/efficiency studies. The new signature has an 8 kHz Level-1 rate allocation, and the emulation tool reports signal efficiency at the allocated rate. A threshold scan over the allowed 20--60 GeV range showed Algorithm-L1 clearly outperforming the other candidates: repeated simulations near the optimum gave about 92.8% signal efficiency at 37 GeV, while Algorithm-L3 was about 85--86% near its optimum and Algorithm-L2 stayed below 80%. This satisfies the efficiency requirement with comfortable margin and uses one of the allowed candidate algorithms. However, I found no project document or tool output that provides the Level-1 FPGA latency for any candidate; candidate_specs.md only states that all candidates fit the FPGA resource budget. Therefore the latency hard requirement cannot be certified from the available evidence and needs latency sign-off before deployment.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: rate_allocation.md gives an 8 kHz allocation. The simulation tool returns efficiency at the allocated rate. In the performed scan, Algorithm-L1 at 37 GeV gave repeated results 92.987%, 92.460%, 92.423%, 93.562%, and 92.756% (mean about 92.8%), exceeding the best observed Algorithm-L3 results (~86%) and Algorithm-L2 results (<80%).

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: candidate_specs.md lists Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3; the recommendation uses Algorithm-L1.

requirements.requirement: The signal efficiency at the allocated rate must be at least 80%.
requirements.evidence: For Algorithm-L1 at 37 GeV, the emulation returned signal efficiencies of 92.987%, 92.460%, 92.423%, 93.562%, and 92.756% in repeated 100000-event runs, all well above 80%.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm's latency on the Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: No available project document or simulation output provides candidate latency. candidate_specs.md states only that all candidates fit the FPGA resource budget in LUTs and DSPs, which does not establish a latency below 4.0 us.
The recommended threshold is 37.0 GeV, within the allowed 20--60 GeV range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L1 at 37.0 GeV.
